newsitem.title: UK: UK opposition leader to urge EU summit referendum.
newsitem.headline: UK opposition leader to urge EU summit referendum.

text.p: The new leader of Britain's opposition Conservative Party will on Friday call for a nationwide referendum on the outcome of next month's European Union summit in Amsterdam, according to British media reports.
William Hague will make the demand because of planned changes to EU rules which will end national vetoes in some areas of decision taking, they said.

Hague was quoted on Independent Television News as planning to tell the annual conference of the Scottish Conservatives: "There can be no excuse for not putting the Amsterdam Treaty to the electorate."
No one was immediately available at party headquarters in London to comment on Hague's speech.

Hague, who won the battle for the Party leadership last week, is in Perth to address his supporters north of the border, a bedraggled band who failed to win a single seat at the May 1 general election.

The conference has already voted to oppose a Scottish Parliament with limited tax-raising powers, which the new Labour government has pledged to set up provided it wins the endorsement of Scottish voters in a referendum.

Hague is expected to argue that if such a constitutional change within Britain justifies a plebiscite, the loss of sovereignty likely to result from the Amsterdam summit similarly requires the endorsement of voters.
The government has already promised a referendum should it recommend that Britain joins a single European currency.
But Hague has already signalled he plans to lead the party in a Eurosceptic direction by saying it will oppose joining a single currency within the next 10 years.
